article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors needs to win over roughly three in four of Iveco’s silent shareholders to reach the 80% acceptance required to complete its €3.9 billion acquisition and delist the Italian truck maker. About 52.9% of Iveco’s common shares, including promoter Exor’s 27%, backed the deal, meaning the company must persuade shareholders owning roughly 27% of the shares who did not vote, while opposition includes 37.27 million votes (13.7% of 271.2 million shares) against Chandrasekaran’s appointment and similar votes against Balaji and Wagh; the offer price was sweetened from €14.10 per share to €14.40 on 9 October. If Tata Motors reaches only the 66.67% threshold it could still complete the tender but would be unable to squeeze out remaining minority shareholders, delist Iveco or carry out the planned demerger, leaving Iveco listed with minority holders; the combined entity is projected to generate annual revenue of about €21 billion and sell over 590,000 vehicles.

Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles (TMCV) is expected to post Q2FY27 revenue growth of around 44‑45% YoY, with JM Financial forecasting Rs 24,218.4 crore (up 43.6% YoY, 25.3% QoQ) and Motilal Oswal Financial Services projecting Rs 24,638.1 crore (up 45.4% YoY). Volume is projected to rise about 43% YoY, with JM estimating 1,35,114 units (up 42.7% YoY, 24.5% QoQ) and MOFSL seeing 1,37,339 units (up 43% YoY, 26.3% sequentially), driven by a 53.1% YoY surge in light commercial vehicles. Adjusted profit‑after‑tax is estimated to increase 44.3% YoY by JM and 25.7% YoY by MOFSL, while margins remain under pressure despite a net price hike of 2.5% since July, making input‑cost inflation, pricing realisation and product mix key monitorables.

Tata Motors' revised €14.40 per share offer to acquire the remaining 80% of Iveco faces a critical test as three investors—Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital and Petrus Advisers—hold about 20.4% of Iveco’s common shares and could earn a combined gain of about €63 million from the buyout, on top of an estimated €288 million in extraordinary dividends received in April. The investors accumulated stakes worth a combined €728 million between July 2025 and September 2026, after Tata announced the deal and before the offer opened on 7 September, and their tender decision will influence whether Tata reaches the 80% threshold needed for full control, with shareholders having tendered about 33.4% of shares as of 21 October and the offer closing on 26 October. Tata’s acquisition, announced in July 2025, includes buying Iveco’s commercial vehicle business for about €3.8 billion after the defence business was sold to Leonardo for an enterprise value of €1.7 billion, and the combined entity would generate annual revenue of about €21 billion and sell more than 590,000 vehicles.

Swiggy reported a consolidated loss after tax of Rs 922 crore for the September quarter, narrowing from Rs 1,092 crore in the year‑ago period but widening sequentially from Rs 792 crore in the June quarter. The loss figures highlight a mixed trend in the company's profitability as investors monitor its September‑quarter earnings.

Tata Motors reported Q2 FY27 consolidated profit of ₹1,257 crore, with revenue rising 36.3% year‑on‑year. The stock fell 3.97 per cent to ₹397.80 on the NSE, opening at ₹410, below its previous close of ₹414.25, and traded between an intraday high of ₹412.70 and a low of ₹392.65.
